targetAudience.primary: Architects and governance engineers designing self-improving digital employees and agent runtimes
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands staged activation, rollback, evaluation gates and stateful tool execution.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A modification can improve forward capability while silently weakening the system’s ability to recover after activation.

whyNow: A primary study reports 197 capability-positive mutations that fail recovery verification, showing that forward improvement and recoverability can diverge at the adoption boundary.

externalHook.description: A self-modification may pass its forward objective yet remain unqualified for recovery under later state evolution.

coreProposition: Capability qualification and recoverability qualification must be independent adoption gates: activation should bind an exact, independently verified recovery bundle for the frozen mutation rather than infer recoverability from forward improvement or the modifying worker’s own account.

originalValue.description: Separates proposal, capability, recovery and activation authority and defines the exact recovery evidence bundle that activation should consume.

readerTakeaway: Freeze the candidate mutation, derive its material effect surface independently, test recovery against counterfactual states and a typed equivalence contract, then bind activation to that exact verified bundle.

supported: The study reports 197 capability-positive candidates that fail recovery verification.
Recovery is evaluated against a frozen mutation, pre-state witness, effect surface, counterfactual states and observational equivalence.
Whole-state restoration can erase legitimate later state in the reported benchmark.
unsupported: Universal rollback for arbitrary enterprise or third-party effects
Independent production validation of the proposed lifecycle
uncertain: How recovery certificates should expire under continuing state drift
How overlapping mutations should share or invalidate effect ownership

firstPartyRole.rationale: The governance boundary stands independently of any first-party project.

decisionReason: The capability/recovery partition and the study’s explicit recovery relation support a concrete adoption-control argument without extending beyond the demonstrated benchmark.
